did_you_know.text: Did you know? At the beginning of the chapter, it is said that the tribe of Dan had not yet received an inheritance among the tribes of Israel, so it searched for a place to settle.
Did you know? The Danites sent five men from Zorah and Eshtaol to spy out the land and explore it; according to the text, they were men of valor.
Did you know? The spies found Laish, a city whose inhabitants lived securely, were relatively isolated from Sidon, and had no dealings with other people.
Did you know? After the spies’ survey, six hundred armed men from the tribe of Dan set out to conquer Laish.
Did you know? The place where the Danites camped near Kiriath-jearim was consequently called Mahaneh-dan, or the Camp of Dan, and the text says that this name remained until its time.
Did you know? The spies discovered an ephod, household idols, a carved image, and a cast image in Micah’s house, and they told their fellow Danites about them before continuing their journey.

Did you know? The Danites took the religious objects from Micah’s house, including the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the cast image, while the six hundred warriors stood at the entrance.
Did you know? The priest joined the Danites after they offered to make him a priest for a tribe and a family in Israel, rather than only for one man’s household.
Did you know? The Danites attacked Laish, killed its inhabitants according to the text, and burned the city; afterward, they rebuilt it and settled there.

Did you know? After settling in Laish, which they renamed Dan, the Danites set up Micah’s carved image there; Jonathan son of Gershom and his descendants served as priests there until the captivity of the land.
